title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
abstract: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, highly sensitive method to search for fifth forces at micron scales using cold atoms trapped in optical tweezer arrays. By employing a quantum-limited homodyne readout protocol, the authors demonstrate a massive improvement in sensitivity, allowing them to probe extra dimensions beyond current experimental capabilities.
main_problem: The paper aims to search for deviations from Newton's law (fifth forces) at micron-range distances, which are predicted by theories involving extra spatial dimensions.
main_result: The proposed method can extend the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints, surpassing current tabletop limits for extra dimensions.
method: The technique involves resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms trapped in an optical tweezer array and using a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry.
model_or_system: The physical system is cold atoms (e.g., $^{171}	ext{Yb}$) confined in an optical tweezer array near a periodic mass source. The theoretical framework models the force deviation using a Yukawa-type potential, and the analysis incorporates concepts from higher-dimensional gravity and Weyl's law.
key_observables: The primary observable is the sideband asymmetry, $R$, or the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), which quantifies the measurement sensitivity to the force coupling constant $\alpha$.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the measurement can approach the Standard Quantum Limit and utilizes approximations like the Born-Markov equation for decay dynamics.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for the force signal, details the advanced homodyne readout protocol using sideband thermometry, calculates the optimal measurement using QFI, and applies this to constrain parameters related to extra dimensions using scaling laws like Weyl's law.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it merges advanced quantum measurement techniques (sideband thermometry, QFI optimization) with fundamental physics searches (fifth forces/extra dimensions) using state-of-the-art AMO platforms (optical tweezer arrays).

An array of optical tweezers is used to confine a two-dimensional grid of atoms at sub- micron range from a thin metallic reflective surface (only a one-dimensional array is shown).
